hypotheses.construction_plan: Instantiate the two-slot kernel K(x,y) generically as K(n,m). For the diagonal branch, specialize y to x so K(x,y) becomes K(n,n). The Piecewise is the confluent assembly that selects the generic evaluation K(n,m) when Ne(n,m) is true, and the diagonal specialization K(n,n) otherwise.
required_assumptions: K is a two-argument function of n and m
Ne(n, m) denotes the inequality condition
proof_obligations: Piecewise((K(n, m), Ne(n, m)), (K(n, n), True)) - Piecewise((K(x, y)[x->n, y->m], Ne(n, m)), (K(x, y)[x->n, y->n], True)) = 0
hypotheses.rationale: The two branches are evaluations of the same two-argument kernel K, with the piecewise condition separating a generic evaluation from its diagonal coalescence. This is structurally a confluent/diagonal specialization pattern.
